description: Level 2 (Grumpstone Ridge): 3 surveys, 2 real blasts and 2 phantom ones, and 5 contract acceptances against a mine that goes formally bankrupt before the first blast ever fires -- named for a $250k win, but `campaign start level:grumpstone_ridge` fails outright (locked) and, under #553's queued, vehicle-gated drilling, the $150,000 budget can no longer fund the 12-person roster staffed:true adds through even the first drilling wait. BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized. fires at tick 132, 205 ticks before blast 1 and long before the operator (per this file's own command sequence) notices or stops; see the pattern-1 drill-wait step and Findings #59-#60 for the full trajectory. Interaction-mode finding, this file's own: once levelEndReason turns non-null at tick 132, LevelEndScreen's full-viewport overlay (z-index 9999, every panel/toolbar control sits at z 100-200) covers the whole screen for the rest of the run and never clears -- no player click reaches ANY panel again after that tick, including blast 1's own charge/sequence/execute and every contract-accept/drill-plan-grid step that follows. Every step past tick 132 that mutates state now runs its command directly (role:'guard' + expect.blocked, same convention this file already used for its phantom blasts) instead of pretending a click still lands. #593 (GameLoop.ts's autoInsertNeedTasks no longer preempting an employee's own interrupted work the instant their rest completes, and VehicleReservation.ts's releaseVehicleReservation now syncing a dismounting driver's real position) changes the trajectory this file records: pattern 1 lands only 23 of its 24 holes before blast 1 fires (2 deaths, not 4, since one driller/rig pair is still short of its hole), which leaves one drill_rig alive to fully drill pattern 2 (25/25) for a second real blast (3 more deaths, 5 total) before patterns 3 and 4 revert to genuinely phantom (both rigs destroyed by blast 2, never replaced). Final balance: -$1,282,536 (#591: updated from -$1,271,073 -- staffed-fleet spawn spacing and vehicle occupancy reroute shift exact pathing/payroll timing without changing the trajectory in kind).

Nothing in the engine stops a `tick` command from continuing to run a level after levelEnded flips (a genuinely pending EVENT, like the Explosive Tariff below, is the only thing that ever halts one), so the mine keeps operating -- legally seized, crew still working -- for the rest of this file.

CI finding, this PR (#586): was role:player driving `resolveEventIfPending`'s real click -- state.levelEndReason has read 'bankruptcy' since tick 132 (8 ticks before this event pends), and the event dialog's own overlay class (`.bs-confirm-overlay`, EventModal.ts) sits at z-index 600, far below `--bsx-z-menu` (9999) that LevelEndScreen's full-viewport overlay has owned since tick 132 -- same class of bug as the Charge/Sequence/blast steps further down this file, just on a dialog instead of a panel, and reached earlier because this event happens to pend this late. Every other 'event choose 0' step in this drilling wait stays role:player safely because `resolveEventIfPending` no-ops (no click at all) when nothing is genuinely pending; this is the one step in the wait where an event really is pending at the moment it runs, so it is the one that actually reaches `resolveEventIfPending`'s bare `page.click('#bs-event-dialog .bs-event-choice')` -- which has no `describeUnclickable` wrapper, so Puppeteer's own unnamed 'Node is either not clickable or not an Element' surfaced instead of a diagnosis. Converted to guard + expect.blocked, command run directly so cash still drops by the tariff. Update: EventModal now also defers behind LevelEndScreen once the level has ended (UIManager.update, matching BlastReportModal's own fix for the same z-index gap) -- its .bs-event-choice buttons are never rendered at all in that state rather than rendered-but-covered, so probing for them reports 'absent', which expect.blocked itself rejects as unprovable (scenario-goal.ts/interaction-driver.ts). The preceding step just ordered a fresh 30-hole drill_plan (5x6 grid); tick 150 in one call processes all of that dispatch/pathfinding in a single blocking page.evaluate, an outlier compared to the tick 20/tick 30 chunks used everywhere else in this project's scenario files. Split into 3x tick 50 -- same total simulation-tick advance, same end state. Update: the split alone did not help -- CI reported the identical "Step 96 timed out after 60000ms" again on the next push, because the step-level timeout (DEFAULT_STEP_TIMEOUT, puppeteer-utils.ts) wraps the WHOLE step's cumulative action time, not each action individually (run-all-scenarios.ts/scenario-interaction-runner.ts both compute stepTimeout once per step and race it against the step's full for-loop of actions). The real fix is this step's own  field (ScenarioStepDef.timeout, seconds, scenario-types.ts) -- raised to 120s, comfortably covering CI's slower/contended runner for this step's genuinely CPU-heavy 150-tick advance right after a fresh 30-hole drill_plan. Kept the 3x tick 50 split too (harmless, and slightly more granular progress if a future step ever needs to interrupt mid-way).
